request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due" total: the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches, added up, or 0.00 when they watch no one. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

This was a front-end change only. The server already reported who each user watches, so no stored data or endpoints changed, and nothing new is written to the audit file.

- **`features/header/counters.slot.tsx`**: adds `watched-due-total`. It adds up each watched person's due-total exactly as that person's row works it out, and leaves out any "n/a", the same way the "My crew due" total does. Unlike the sheet's own due-total, it doesn't drop the highest and lowest figures.
- **`features/people/watch.slot.tsx`**: the existing `useWatched` hook (the list of people this user watches) is now exported so the header can use it.

Each user sees their own figure: in the test, Uma and Vic watch different people and see different totals.
